scenario.name: Microsoft Purview DFIR, CISA & MITRE — M365 Purview New-ComplianceSearch & eDiscovery Export Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a modern glass office building where visitors check in with the front-desk receptionist, scan a badge at the lobby turnstile, and walk between glass-walled meeting rooms. In the sunlit office building lobby, an unbadged visitor talks past the front-desk receptionist and persuades the desk clerk to print a temporary building pass. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lobby badge turnstile in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the lobby badge turnstile in tiny disguised batches. When building security compares the receptionist sign-in sheet against the turnstile badge swipes across the glass offices, the unescorted hallway trail is exposed. In this scenario (T1098.003, Microsoft Purview DFIR, CISA & MITRE, M365 Purview New-ComplianceSearch & eDiscovery Export Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: roleGroupMember Added to eDiscovery Manager, then tenant-Wide Keyword Query, then pST/Zip Package Export. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering RoleGroupMember Added to eDiscovery Manager, then Tenant-Wide Keyword Query, then PST/Zip Package Export, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1098.003 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: RoleGroupMember Added to eDiscovery Manager in Security & Compliance Center
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1098.003 - Additional Cloud Roles)
stages.description: In the sunlit office building lobby, an unbadged visitor talks past the front-desk receptionist and persuades the desk clerk to print a temporary building pass. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lobby badge turnstile in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the front-desk receptionist go about their routine. To read mailboxes and SharePoint sites without modifying individual mailbox permissions, the compromised admin adds an account to the eDiscovery Manager role group (Add-RoleGroupMember / Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin), logged in the Unified Audit Log (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with AuditWorkload=SecurityComplianceCenter, Operation=Add-RoleGroupMember , eDiscovery Manager, TargetAccount=admin_clark@corp.local so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations "Add-RoleGroupMember","Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations "Add-RoleGroupMember","Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin" via Syste so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1098.003 during "RoleGroupMember Added to eDiscovery Manager in Security & Compliance Center" , To read mailboxes and SharePoint sites without modifying individual mailbox permissions, the compromised admin adds an account to the eDiscovery Manager role group , Add-RoleGroupMember / Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin, logged in the Unified Audit Log while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Get-RoleGroupMember -Identity "eDiscovery Manager" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Get-RoleGroupMember -Identity "eDiscovery Manager" via System / Runtime Execution Interface so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1098.003 during "RoleGroupMember Added to eDiscovery Manager in Security & Compliance Center" , To read mailboxes and SharePoint sites without modifying individual mailbox permissions, the compromised admin adds an account to the eDiscovery Manager role group , Add-RoleGroupMember / Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin, logged in the Unified Audit Log while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: Tenant-Wide Keyword Query via New-ComplianceSearch & Start-ComplianceSearch
stages.subtitle: Collection (T1213.002 - Data from Information Repositories: SharePoint)
stages.description: Instead of staying in the public waiting chairs, the visitor taps that pass at the lobby turnstile and walks down the hallway from one glass meeting room to the next. Here in Step 2 inside the office building, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the front-desk receptionist's station without disturbing the public lobby waiting area. Connecting via Connect-IPPSSession, the actor executes New-ComplianceSearch with -ExchangeLocation All -SharePointLocation All and a ContentMatchQuery targeting password, key, vpn, or acquisition keywords, generating SearchCreated and SearchStarted audit records (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with AuditOperation=SearchCreated / New-ComplianceSearch, SearchScope=ExchangeLocation: All, SharePointLocation: All, KeywordQuery=password OR client_secret so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations "New-ComplianceSearch","Start-ComplianceSearch","SearchCreated" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations "New-ComplianceSearch","Start-ComplianceSearch","SearchCr so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1213.002 during "Tenant-Wide Keyword Query via New-ComplianceSearch & Start-ComplianceSearch" , Connecting via Connect-IPPSSession, the actor executes New-ComplianceSearch with -ExchangeLocation All -SharePointLocation All and a ContentMatchQuery targeting password, key, vpn, or acquisition keywords, generating SearchCreated and SearchStarted audit records while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Get-ComplianceSearch | Select-Object Name,CreatedBy,ContentMatchQuery,Status runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Get-ComplianceSearch | Select-Object Name,CreatedBy,ContentMatchQuery,Status via System / Ru so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1213.002 during "Tenant-Wide Keyword Query via New-ComplianceSearch & Start-ComplianceSearch" , Connecting via Connect-IPPSSession, the actor executes New-ComplianceSearch with -ExchangeLocation All -SharePointLocation All and a ContentMatchQuery targeting password, key, vpn, or acquisition keywords, generating SearchCreated and SearchStarted audit records while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ New-ComplianceSearch -Name "Audit_Check_Q4" -ExchangeLocation All -SharePointLocation All -ContentMatchQuery "password OR client_secret" / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Security & Compliance PowerShell (IPPS)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Exchange Mailboxes & SharePoint Sites).

stages.title: Stage 3: PST/Zip Package Export via New-ComplianceSearchAction -Export & SearchExported Audit
stages.subtitle: Exfiltration (T1114.002 - Remote Email Collection)
stages.description: Inside the executive glass conference room, the intruder opens the unlocked cabinet and copies private project folders while staff walk by outside thinking they belong there. In this final step inside the office building, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lobby badge turnstile in tiny disguised batches until the reception sign-in logbook catches the mismatch. Once the search completes, the actor runs New-ComplianceSearchAction -SearchName "Audit_Check_Q4" -Export to stage a downloadable PST and SharePoint ZIP archive in the Microsoft-managed Azure Blob export container, triggering a high-severity SearchExported event (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with AuditOperation=SearchExported , New-ComplianceSearchAction -Export, SearchJobName=Audit_Check_Q4, ExportedItemCount=1,840 items so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations "New-ComplianceSearchAction","SearchExported","PreviewSearch" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations "New-ComplianceSearchAction","SearchExported","PreviewSea so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1114.002 during "PST/Zip Package Export via New-ComplianceSearchAction -Export & SearchExported Audit" , Once the search completes, the actor runs New-ComplianceSearchAction -SearchName "Audit_Check_Q4" -Export to stage a downloadable PST and SharePoint ZIP archive in the Microsoft-managed Azure Blob export container, triggering a high-severity SearchExported event while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Remove-ComplianceSearch -Identity "Audit_Check_Q4" -Confirm:$false runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Remove-ComplianceSearch -Identity "Audit_Check_Q4" -Confirm:$false via System / Runtime Exec so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1114.002 during "PST/Zip Package Export via New-ComplianceSearchAction -Export & SearchExported Audit" , Once the search completes, the actor runs New-ComplianceSearchAction -SearchName "Audit_Check_Q4" -Export to stage a downloadable PST and SharePoint ZIP archive in the Microsoft-managed Azure Blob export container, triggering a high-severity SearchExported event while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ New-ComplianceSearchAction -SearchName "Audit_Check_Q4" -Export -Format FxStream / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 Security & Compliance PowerShell (IPPS)) to Node ④ (#4 Purview eDiscovery Case Engine), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Exchange Mailboxes & SharePoint Sites).

keySpecs.value: Create a high-severity Microsoft Defender XDR / Sentinel alert rule on UnifiedAuditLog Operations SearchExported and New-ComplianceSearchAction (-Export), and immediately purge unauthorized compliance search jobs.
